notes: TWAS expression preprocessing kernels. Per-column stateful average-tie rank scan replaced with OpenMP across columns + std::sort + tight tie-resolution loop. INT path: C++ produces u = (rank-c)/(n-2c+1) per column; Python applies sqrt(2)*erfinv(2u-1) via torch (vectorised). Quantile-norm path: Python precomputes reference = sorted_x.mean(dim=1); C++ scatters reference[i] back via column-wise tie-resolved index. Both bench against random Gaussian inputs.
scaling: Both scale linearly with n_genes (number of independent column problems). At GTEx-scale (n=200 × m=20K), INT moves from 18.7s to 11.2ms; quantile-norm from 35.0s to 16.2ms.
